metadata.title: Patient Intake API — CGE-P Capstone Component Definition

components.title: Patient Intake API (governed)
components.description: The starter Patient Intake API (VPC + Lambda + API Gateway v2 + DynamoDB + S3) after the four CGE-P layers have been applied. This component-definition asserts, for each SOC 2 TSC control in scope, which Terraform resource and Rego policy pair implements the control and where the Cosign-signed evidence lands.
components.purpose: Ingest patient intake submissions (PHI) over HTTPS and persist them to DynamoDB and S3 under customer-managed KMS keys, with a continuous evidence trail suitable for SOC 2 Type II attestation.

control-implementations.description: SOC 2 Type II Trust Services Criteria (2022) — community OSCAL catalog, pinned at commit ea49c4c05c8c62098b3766fd8f26b862fb5181f4. See oscal/README.md for pin rationale and fallback plan.

implemented-requirements.description: **CC6.1 — Logical access controls.** All PHI-bearing data stores are encrypted at rest with a customer-managed KMS key (CMK). Terraform provisions `aws_kms_key.data` and wires it into `terraform/main.tf:aws_dynamodb_table.intake` (via `server_side_encryption { enabled = true, kms_key_arn = aws_kms_key.data.arn }`) and `terraform/main.tf:aws_s3_bucket.uploads` (via a companion `aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.uploads` with `sse_algorithm = "aws:kms"`). The Rego policy `policies/soc2/cc6/kms_on_data_stores.rego` fails the CI pipeline if any bucket or table is planned without a CMK reference. Closes GAP-01 and GAP-02.

**CC6.3 — Authorization: least privilege.** The Lambda execution role's inline policy is scoped to enumerated actions on specific resource ARNs (never `*:*`). Terraform tightens `terraform/main.tf:aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_inline` to `{dynamodb:PutItem, dynamodb:GetItem}` on the intake table ARN and `{s3:PutObject, s3:GetObject}` on the uploads bucket ARN. The Rego policy `policies/soc2/cc6/least_priv_iam.rego` denies any IAM policy containing `Action:"*"` or a service-wildcard like `dynamodb:*`. Closes GAP-07.

**CC6.6 — Boundary protection.** The Lambda function runs inside the workload VPC's private subnets. Terraform adds `vpc_config { subnet_ids = aws_subnet.private[*].id, security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.lambda.id] }` to `terraform/main.tf:aws_lambda_function.intake`. The security group's egress is scoped to VPC endpoints only (S3 gateway endpoint + DynamoDB gateway endpoint). The Rego policy `policies/soc2/cc6/lambda_in_vpc.rego` fails the plan if any Lambda has an empty `vpc_config`. Closes GAP-05.

**CC6.7 — Transmission security.** Every S3 bucket (uploads + evidence vault) has a companion `aws_s3_bucket_policy` denying requests where `aws:SecureTransport=false`. Terraform provisions these as `terraform/main.tf:aws_s3_bucket_policy.uploads_tls_only` and `terraform/grc_evidence.tf:aws_s3_bucket_policy.evidence_tls_only`. In transit, the API Gateway v2 stage's DNS-facing endpoint is HTTPS-only (AWS-managed). The Rego policy `policies/soc2/cc6/tls_only_bucket_policy.rego` fails the plan if any bucket is missing its TLS-only policy. Closes GAP-03.

**CC7.2 — System monitoring: detection.** Three detection surfaces are provisioned: (1) `terraform/grc_cloudtrail.tf:aws_cloudtrail.governance` — multi-region trail with `enable_log_file_validation = true`, logs to a dedicated KMS-encrypted S3 bucket with lifecycle to Glacier at 90 days; (2) `terraform/main.tf:aws_apigatewayv2_stage.default` gets an `access_log_settings` block writing to a CloudWatch log group; (3) `terraform/main.tf:aws_lambda_function.intake` gets `dead_letter_config { target_arn = aws_sqs_queue.dlq.arn }` and `tracing_config { mode = "Active" }` (X-Ray). The Rego policy `policies/soc2/cc7/detection_enabled.rego` denies the plan if any of the three is missing or weaker than required. Closes GAP-06 and GAP-08.

**CC8.1 — Change management.** Every change to the workload lands via a pull request that is gated by `.github/workflows/grc-gate.yml`. The gate runs `terraform plan`, then `opa test policies/` (policy suite unit tests), then `conftest test --all-namespaces --parser json --policy policies/ plan.json`. Any policy deny causes the pipeline to fail and blocks merge. On successful merge to `main`, the pipeline applies the plan and produces a Cosign-signed evidence bundle uploaded to the Object Lock evidence vault. The bundle contains the plan, filtered state summary, policy results, and a manifest binding the commit SHA. This is the primary CC8.1 evidence surface — every merged change has a signed, WORM-retained artefact proving what changed and that the gate passed. Cross-cutting; no single Terraform resource address applies.

**A1.2 — Availability: backups and recovery.** The evidence vault S3 bucket has both versioning enabled and Object Lock in Compliance mode with a default retention of 365 days. Terraform provisions `terraform/grc_evidence.tf:aws_s3_bucket.evidence` (with `object_lock_enabled = true`), `aws_s3_bucket_versioning.evidence` (`status = "Enabled"`), and `aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration.evidence` (`rule.default_retention.days = 365`, `mode = "COMPLIANCE"`). The uploads bucket also has versioning enabled. The Rego policy `policies/soc2/a1/object_lock_and_versioning.rego` fails the plan if the evidence bucket lacks either. Closes GAP-04.
